text:
jordan: FYI rolling BMC firmware batch in ap-northeast1 caused about ~60 nodes to flip UEFI lockdown unexpectedly. OOB sessions drop, provisioner backlog spiked, GPU pool capacity down ~8%. runbook: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/bmc-rollout>
lee: ugh. did the canary fail or was this in the middle of cohort 3? any obvious error logs from the BMC?
sam: canary looked fine for cohort 1/2. Cohort 3 started at 10:18 UTC and we started seeing `oob: session closed` across multiple racks ~10:21 UTC.
ops-bot: ALERT: provisioning-backlog ap-northeast1 exceeded threshold (5m avg backlog 240 -> 980). Pager duty notified.
arun: suggest isolating the affected racks from the rollout and reassigning their workloads to reserved spare pool. We should avoid evicting more GPUs to on-demand if possible.
morgan: cost note: autoscaler pulled ~22 on-demand GPUs in the last 12 mins; that's ~+$2.7k/hr if we don't stabilize soon. tagging billing alerts.
tina: trying a targeted rescind for cohort-3 firmware job now: `ci-deploy rollback bmc-fw --cohort=3 --dry-run=false --reason="uefi-lockdown-flip"`
jordan: ran the rollback on the firmware job and paused the pipeline. also ran `oob-reconnect --nodes @affected` against a subset, but saw `kv-cache epoch mismatch` on the agent side for ~12 nodes.
sam: can you paste a small sample of node ids with the error so infra can triage? put them in a code block.
jordan: sure

```
rack-apn1-34-201
rack-apn1-34-203
rack-apn1-37-009
rack-apn1-37-011
rack-apn1-40-120
```

lee: escalating to firmware team, raising a P1 and handing off logs. tagging @firmware on the runbook page.
deploy-bot: Deployment pipeline paused: bmc-fw-rollout (id: fw-2026-03-20-0930). Cohort 3 rollback initiated by tina.
morgan: please estimate SLA / customer impact. Any queued customer requests failing or just internal provisioning retries?
arun: current symptom: most customer-facing endpoints still healthy — frontend caches served on-memory. The problem is delayed provisioning of new jobs and longer queue times for scheduled batches. If rollback finishes quickly, we should recover without user-facing errors.
tina: I propagated a small hotfix script to resync KV epoch on affected agents: `scripts/resync-kv --nodes @affected --force`. Running dry-run then apply.
jordan: applied resync to 6/12 nodes, OOB sessions re-established for 4/6. Two nodes still fail with `watchdog not responding` in BMC logs. I'm isolating those and marking them for manual reflash.
lee: good. keep the pipeline paused until firmware team signs off. we should also add an automated pre-check for UEFI lockdown bit after flash in the rollout pipeline.
arun: agree — add precheck + metrics so we don't hit this silent flip again. I'll file a follow-up ticket.
ops-bot: RECOVERY: provisioning-backlog ap-northeast1 reduced to 180 (5m avg). Auto-escalation cleared.
jordan: monitoring shows capacity trending back up, autoscaler already returned 16 of 22 on-demand nodes. keeping this thread open for the manual reflashes and postmortem.
